title: Grim Feast Guide — Grim Remnants, Minion Revival and the Reworked Skill
summary: Grim Feast no longer restores Energy Shield — in the current 0.5.4 client it is a Spirit gem that turns fallen minions into Grim Remnants, each storing a portion of the minion's Life, and can revive minions through Grim Resurrection. This guide explains why old build guides are obsolete, which minions create remnants, how much Life is stored, how revival chooses which minions return, the 30 Spirit cost, Quality, the 0.5 cooldown change, and the mapping / bossing rotations used by Lich, Infernalist and Gemling minion builds.
description: Grim Feast deep guide: the rework from ES remnant to minion remnant / revive, which minions generate remnants, stored Life per remnant and the cap, Grim Resurrection order and limits, 30 Spirit budget, Quality storage ratio, persistent supports, mapping collection and bossing mass-death handling, troubleshooting (no remnant, no revive, expired) and real community questions answered directly.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Quick Answer: It Revives Minions, Not Energy Shield
paragraphs: In the current client Grim Feast does NOT restore Energy Shield. It is a Spirit gem that converts fallen minions into Grim Remnants and can bring minions back through Grim Resurrection.
Every old 'ES overflow' build guide is obsolete. If you are following a pre-0.3 guide for Grim Feast, discard it and use the minion-revival version.

sections.title: Old Version vs Current Version
paragraphs: Before the rework, Grim Feast produced Energy Shield remnants / overflow and was a defensive tool. That design is gone.

From 0.3 onward Grim Feast is a minion tool: dead minions leave Grim Remnants that store Life, and Grim Resurrection spends them to revive minions. The 0.5 patch added a resurrection cooldown and bug fixes that change how aggressively you can revive.
bullets: 0.5: Grim Resurrection cooldown + bug fixes (operation limits).

sections.title: Requirements and Setup
paragraphs: Grim Feast needs Reviving Minions — minions that, on death, leave a Grim Remnant the skill can later spend. Minions that simply dissolve on death without a remnant do not feed the revival loop.
It is a Spirit gem, so it competes with other persistent buffs for your 30 Spirit reservation. You enable it once and it runs in the background.

keyValues.label: Minions
notes: Only reviving minions leave usable remnants.

sections.title: Persistent Buff and Spirit
paragraphs: Grim Feast is a persistent buff: once enabled it stays active and reserves 30 Spirit for the whole map. You do not recast it; you manage it through Spirit budget and revival timing.
Because it is always on, the value is in what it does passively — collecting remnants and enabling Grim Resurrection — not in active casting.

keyValues.label: Reservation
notes: Count it against your total Spirit pool.

keyValues.label: State
notes: No recast; manage via revival timing.

sections.title: Remnants and Grim Resurrection
paragraphs: When a Reviving Minion dies it drops a Grim Remnant storing a portion of its Life. Grim Resurrection consumes remnants to bring minions back, but it does not revive every minion at once — it revives a subset, and the order is determined by the remnant queue, not by which minion you 'want' back.

If many minions die together (common in boss fights), the revival only covers what the stored Life can pay for, so some minions stay dead until more remnants accumulate. The 0.5 patch added a resurrection cooldown, so you cannot spam revival every frame.

keyValues.label: Per remnant
notes: Verify the exact stored percentage on client 0.5.4.

keyValues.label: Revival
notes: Not all minions return at once; order follows the remnant queue.

keyValues.label: Cooldown
notes: Grim Resurrection now has an operation cooldown.

sections.title: Spirit Budget Trade-offs
paragraphs: Grim Feast costs 30 Spirit, the same pool used by Herald buffs, auras and other persistent minion supports. On a minion build you must decide whether the revival safety net is worth more than an extra aura or damage buff.
Most minion builds that already run Reviving Minions keep Grim Feast, but tight-Spirit builds may drop it for more damage.

keyValues.label: Trade-off
notes: Drop it only if Spirit is the bottleneck.

sections.title: Quality
paragraphs: Quality on Grim Feast increases the portion of minion Life stored per remnant, so higher quality means each remnant revives more or revives minions more reliably.
Verify the exact quality roll on the current client; it scales the stored-Life ratio, not the revival count directly.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: Persistent supports that boost minion survival or additive minion damage pair well, since Grim Feast is itself a persistent minion buff. Clarity and other Spirit-affecting supports indirectly help by easing the reservation pressure.
Avoid supports that assume you actively cast the gem — Grim Feast is enabled, not spammed.

keyValues.label: Persistent minion supports
notes: Stack with the persistent revival theme.

sections.title: Where It Is Used
paragraphs: Lich and Infernalist minion builds use Grim Feast as a revival safety net so their army stays alive through map and boss attrition. Gemling Legionnaire variants use it when they already run Reviving Minions and can spare the 30 Spirit.
In every case the build values the passive revival more than the lost damage aura.
bullets: Infernalist: keeps the army alive through attrition.
Gemling Legionnaire: revival when Spirit allows.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: The biggest community trap is following pre-0.3 'ES overflow' guides for Grim Feast — they describe a skill that no longer exists. Client testing confirms the current version is minion revival only.

The 0.5 'sometimes will not revive' reports are mostly the new resurrection cooldown plus the subset limitation, not a hard bug; waiting out the cooldown and accumulating remnants resolves most cases.
